swap_risks: CRITICAL SUPPLY VOLTAGE RATING: MC33202DR2G is limited to 12 V max (13 V abs max, p.3) whereas LM2904DR supports up to 26 V (26 V abs max, p.4). Installing a 5.5 V CMOS part on a 12 V–24 V rail causes instant breakdown.

HIGH HEADROOM / CLIPPING RISK: Rail-to-rail capability differs (LM2904DR: IN=Non-RR, OUT=Non-RR vs MC33202DR2G: IN=RR, OUT=RR); verify input common-mode range (Vicm) and output voltage swing against ADC full-scale range.

CAUTION BANDWIDTH & PHASE MARGIN: GBWP differs by 3.1x (LM2904DR: 0.7 MHz p.11 vs MC33202DR2G: 2.2 MHz p.4); higher-bandwidth replacements can oscillate with capacitive loads or stray feedback capacitance without an isolation resistor.
CAUTION SLEW RATE DIFFERENCE: Slew rate differs by 3.3x (LM2904DR: 0.3 V/µs p.11 vs MC33202DR2G: 1 V/µs p.4); check full-power bandwidth SR / (2π·Vpeak).

CAUTION QUIESCENT CURRENT SHIFT: Supply current per channel differs by 2.6x (LM2904DR: 350 µA/ch p.11 vs MC33202DR2G: 900 µA/ch p.4); verify battery budget and total power dissipation across all channels.
HIGH ABSOLUTE-MAX SURGE MARGIN: MC33202DR2G has a lower Vs,abs,max rating (13 V, p.3) than LM2904DR (26 V, p.4); verify hot-plug, inductive kickback, and TVS clamp peaks stay safely below 13 V.
HIGH THERMAL MARGIN: Package θJA is 52% higher on MC33202DR2G (LM2904DR: 124.7 °C/W p.5 vs MC33202DR2G: 190 °C/W p.5); re-check Tj = Ta + Pd × θJA against Tj,max.
HIGH MINIMUM SUPPLY FLOOR: LM2904DR requires Vs,min >= 3 V (p.5) vs 1.8 V on the counterpart; confirm low-battery / brown-out operation still clears the higher floor.

HIGH TEMPERATURE GRADE MISMATCH: Rated ambient range differs (LM2904DR: -40..125 °C Extended Industrial / Automotive Temp (-40°C to +125°C TA) vs MC33202DR2G: -40..105 °C Extended Industrial (-40°C to 105°C)); MC33202DR2G hot limit only 105 °C — verify product ambient qualification before swapping.
engineering_verdict: LM2904DR (Texas Instruments, SOIC-8) and MC33202DR2G (onsemi, SOIC-8) are Level 2 Functional / Tuning Required alternatives: the PCB land pattern is compatible, but passive retuning or rating derating is mandatory because supply voltage Vs,max drops >=20%; rail-to-rail input/output swing differs; GBWP differs 3.1x. Signal-chain deltas: GBWP 0.7 MHz (p.11) vs 2.2 MHz (p.4), supply ceiling 26 V (p.5) vs 12 V (p.1), Vos 7 mV (p.11) vs 8 mV (p.3), Ib 4x gap (20000 vs 80000 pA), voltage noise 40 vs 20 nV/√Hz. Primary bench gotchas to watch: LM2904DR "Hidden 26 V Supply Ceiling Trap When Swapping From 30 V/32 V LM358DR to 'Extended-Temp' LM2904DR!" (p.4) and MC33202DR2G "Internal Back-to-Back Differential Input Clamp Diodes Limit Comparator Use" (p.3). BOM decision: Choose LM2904DR when supply rails exceed 12 V (rated up to 26 V) or ultra-low supply current (350 µA/ch) is prioritized; choose MC33202DR2G when closed-loop signal bandwidth requires 2.2 MHz GBWP or single-supply ADC headroom demands full Rail-to-Rail I/O swing. Always verify Pin 1 orientation (TOP_VIEW p.3 vs TOP_VIEW p.2) and official datasheets on hardware prototypes prior to production.
